title: Energy Storage Growth Surge Goes Global: Three Things to Know | BloombergNEF
gist: BloombergNEF projects record global energy storage additions of 188GW/535GWh in 2026 (+45% y/y in GW), led by China, the US and Australia, with India adding 26x more batteries than last year, followed by another record of 209GW/638GWh in 2027. Protectionist localization policies in the US, EU and Japan are pushing Chinese equipment suppliers toward the Middle East, Latin America and Sub-Saharan Africa, while solar curtailment and co-location mandates keep renewables-plus-storage growing.

insights.claim: BloombergNEF forecasts global energy storage additions of a record 188GW (535GWh) in 2026, 45% year-on-year growth in gigawatts, with 62% installed in China, the US and Australia.
insights.so_what: Battery storage demand is accelerating, supporting volumes for cell makers, integrators and LFP supply chains.
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: BloombergNEF expects global storage additions to set another record in 2027, growing 11% in gigawatts to 209GW/638GWh as deployment broadens beyond today's largest markets.
insights.so_what: Growth decelerates from 45% to 11% in 2027, so the next leg depends on newer markets rather than China/US.
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: BloombergNEF projects cumulative global energy storage capacity to grow 10-fold from 2025 levels to 3 terawatts, or 11 terawatt-hours, by 2036.
insights.so_what: A decade-long structural demand runway for stationary storage.
insights.quote: Cumulative storage capacity grows 10-fold to 3 terawatts or 11 terawatt-hours in 2036 from 2025 levels.
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: Energy storage growth is driven by rising solar penetration, storage-pairing mandates and fiscal incentive programs, according to BloombergNEF.
insights.so_what: Monitor solar penetration and mandate/incentive policy changes as leading indicators for storage demand.
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: China's energy storage build in 2026 is surprisingly strong despite last year's phaseout of a mandate requiring storage for renewables, supported by a new firming requirement for standalone solar and wind projects and a renewed 300GW storage deployment target by 2030.
insights.so_what: Chinese policy replaced the old mandate quickly, reducing downside risk for Chinese storage demand.
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: US energy storage build stays strong thanks to preserved tax credits and is accelerated by on-site storage demand from data centers.
insights.so_what: AI/data center buildout is an additional demand driver for US battery storage.
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: India's tender-driven annual energy storage additions will top 6GW in 2026, up from a few hundred megawatts last year, about 26 times more batteries than the previous year.
insights.so_what: India is becoming a major new storage market for suppliers.
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: Australia will almost double its annual energy storage additions in 2026, and in Europe countries beyond the UK, Germany and Italy, including Bulgaria, Romania, Poland, France, Greece, the Netherlands and Ukraine, reach gigawatt-scale additions.
insights.so_what: European storage demand is broadening geographically, widening the opportunity set for developers.
insights.locator: Beyond the UK, Germany and Italy
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: Spain, the United Arab Emirates, Chile and Japan accelerate storage build in 2027 on power market fundamentals, diversified revenue stacks and utility-led procurement, and by 2036 growth shifts to Latin America, Sub-Saharan Africa, Southeast Asia and other European countries.
insights.so_what: Long-term storage growth will come from emerging regions rather than current leaders.
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: Sodium-ion batteries are gaining traction in storage after recent increases in lithium iron phosphate material prices, offering lower fire risk and a wide operating temperature range that reduces the need for liquid cooling.
insights.so_what: Higher LFP material prices make sodium-ion more attractive; watch sodium-ion supplier scale-up.
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: BloombergNEF expects lithium iron phosphate (LFP) to remain the main energy storage chemistry over the next decade due to cost competitiveness, high cycle life and supply chain dominance, while sodium-ion and other non-lithium long-duration storage are held back by limited manufacturing scale and cost.
insights.so_what: Alternative chemistries remain niche; LFP incumbents keep their position.
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: The US leads moves to localize battery storage supply chains with tariffs and incentives for domestic production, while restricting equipment that relies on China-linked supply chains; cybersecurity and supply-chain security concerns are guiding similar policies in the EU and Japan.
insights.so_what: Non-Chinese battery storage manufacturers benefit from protected markets in the US, EU and Japan.
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: Because of trade barriers in the US, EU and Japan, Chinese energy storage equipment providers are turning to less restricted markets such as the Middle East, Latin America and Sub-Saharan Africa.
insights.so_what: Expect stronger price competition from Chinese suppliers in emerging markets.
insights.locator: With these barriers, Chinese equipment providers
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: South Korea, India and Brazil also have protectionist battery storage policies, but they are less stringent than those in the US.
insights.so_what: These markets stay partly open to Chinese suppliers.
insights.locator: With these barriers, Chinese equipment providers
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: By the end of 2025, 69GW/196GWh of energy storage had been paired with 299GW of solar globally, driven by growing solar curtailment and price cannibalization in markets such as the US, Australia and Chile.
insights.so_what: Solar curtailment and price cannibalization are a structural driver of hybrid solar-plus-storage projects.
insights.speaker: dsimon110

insights.claim: Although China's co-location mandate for batteries with renewables is expiring, nine other countries including India, Mexico and the Philippines have regulatory or auction-linked co-location mandates, and BloombergNEF expects renewable-plus-storage deployment to stay robust over the next few years.
insights.so_what: Hybrid renewables-plus-storage demand is supported by policy in many markets.
insights.speaker: dsimon110
